word_order: SVO | Sentences consistently place a subject before a verb and objects/complements after the verb (e.g., "Stars give off light": Stars [S] give [V] off light [O]).
register: Formal edited written prose (encyclopedic / informational style, not spontaneous speech).
notes_for_prompt_writer: Prefer splitting at explicit clause-connectors (and, but, while, although, when, because, etc.) but avoid committing a segment when the token is a preposition or complementizer (to, of, that, which, 's) that likely continues a phrase. Be conservative near infinitive markers and possessives — these often look like boundaries but are not. The source is formal written English and contains long, multi-clausal sentences and parenthetical material; aim to emit syntactically coherent chunks (complete clause or clause group) to preserve meaning and avoid premature translation errors.
